original_question: For d = 1 and s in (1/2, 3/2), in the critical Lieb-Thirring inequality for ( -Delta)^s, is the optimal constant equal to the corresponding one-particle constant?
target_in_paper: The nearest paper-faithful target is the sharp-constant discussion of the generalized/fractional Lieb–Thirring conjecture, specialized to the one-dimensional critical line γ = 1 - 1/(2s): namely, whether the optimal constant L_{1-1/(2s),1,s} equals the corresponding one-particle constant L^{(1)}_{1-1/(2s),1,s} for 1/2 < s < 3/2. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right dimension d = 1, the right fractional kinetic operator (-Δ)^s, the right critical regime in the sense of the critical Lieb–Thirring exponent, and the right comparison target: the many-body sharp constant versus the one-particle constant. It is also narrowly aimed at the conjectural sharp-constant question rather than a broader neighboring problem. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y))
missing_details: The critical exponent should be stated explicitly: γ = 1 - 1/(2s), so the inequality in question is the critical fractional Lieb–Thirring inequality in which the power of V_- on the right-hand side is exactly 1. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y))

The precise sharp-constant inequality should be written out: Tr(((-Δ)^s + V)_-)^{γ} ≤ L_{γ,1,s} ∫_R V_-(x) dx with γ = 1 - 1/(2s). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y))
The operator should be anchored on L^2(R), with (-Δ)^s understood as the fractional Laplacian on the line.
The potential class should be made explicit: V should be real-valued on R and satisfy V_- ∈ L^1(R).

The phrase 'one-particle constant' should be defined explicitly as the optimal constant L^{(1)}_{γ,1,s} in the corresponding one-bound-state/lowest-eigenvalue inequality, not merely mentioned informally.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether the equality of constants holds for every s in the open interval (1/2, 3/2).

It helps to state why this is the relevant range: in this window the conjectural sharp scenario is the one-particle branch rather than the semiclassical branch. ([f08.uni-stuttgart.de](https://www.f08.uni-stuttgart.de/.content/media/downloads/Mathematik/mathematische_berichte/2004/2004-017.pdf?utm_source=openai))
The draft does not distinguish the equality of optimal constants from any claim about existence, uniqueness, or structure of optimizers; the paper-level question concerns the constants.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the generalized sharp-constant conjecture L_{γ,d,s} = max{L^{cl}_{γ,d,s}, L^{(1)}_{γ,d,s}}, does the one-dimensional critical fractional case d = 1, γ = 1 - 1/(2s), 1/2 < s < 3/2 lie entirely on the one-particle branch, so that L_{1-1/(2s),1,s} = L^{(1)}_{1-1/(2s),1,s}? ([f08.uni-stuttgart.de](https://www.f08.uni-stuttgart.de/.content/media/downloads/Mathematik/mathematische_berichte/2004/2004-017.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This rewrite stays close to your draft but makes it fully stand-alone by inserting the exact critical exponent, the exact inequality, the operator and function-space setting, the potential assumptions, and the exact meaning of 'one-particle constant'. It does not broaden the problem beyond the paper’s sharp-constant discussion: it is precisely the fractional/generalized Lieb–Thirring conjecture specialized to d = 1 at the critical line, where the right-hand side becomes an L^1 norm of V_-. The interval 1/2 < s < 3/2 is also not cosmetic; it is the range in which the conjectural sharp constant is expected to be the one-particle one rather than the semiclassical one. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y))
